transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-08 16:00 PST | Duration 47m | Redwood: Maya Chen, Owen Patel | Pioneer: Lena Ortiz (CTO), Samir Khan (Lead ML Eng), Ava Brooks (SRE), Diego Ruiz (PM)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll do a 1 minute intro, i'm maya, i'm the AE on this account, with me is owen, our solutions engineer, um quick agenda: parity map, console walkthrough, and perf/cost tradeoffs and security.
[00:18] Lena: thanks, maya. we mostly want to understand what changes for our endpoints - we're on openai/gpt4 + anthropic claude for some tasks and together for some embeddings. main asks: latency < 80ms p95 on short chat, cost lower by 20%, and SOC2 proof.
[00:36] Owen: great, we'll focus on those. quick note - when we say "Redwood Dedicated" sometimes transcription shows "Redwood dedcated" in notes, ignore that.
[00:45] Diego: haha noted. also curious about tokenization - we've seen different token counts across providers and it skews cost.
[00:52] Owen: yep, so first slide — parity_matrix.xlsx (we'll share) maps OpenAI/Anthropic/Together models to Redwood equivalents. for example, OpenAI gpt-4 -> rdx-4-ish (quant variants) and Claude-instruct -> rdx-instruct-legacy. these are loose names, but the matrix has exact endpoints and sample prompts.
[01:12] Samir: can you show a sample curl for how to call our existing endpoints translated to redwood? our infra team needs exact header changes and streaming differences.
[01:20] Maya: yes, we'll attach example curl/snippets. owen, do console demo?
[01:25] Owen: sure. switching screens — opening console, routes page — you can pin model versions per route, set rollout policy for canary, and add automatic fallback to a cheaper quantized variant.
[01:40] [screen share noise/typing]
[02:05] Owen: note on streaming: Redwood supports chunked streaming similar to event-streams; small differences in SSE framing that your client lib needs to handle, we'll include a streaming shim for node/python. sometimes the auto-transcription shows "S S E" as other letters, ignore.
[02:28] Ava: our SREs care about network topology — can Redwood run inside our VPC or do we punch out? we need to keep traffic inside our private networks if possible.
[02:36] Maya: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC peering and a private control plane. for air-gapped/on-prem we have a package too, but that's enterprise.
[02:50] Lena: and for keys, KMS? we mandate customer-managed keys.
[02:55] Owen: supported — KMS/HSM integrations. audit logs show per-request metadata and token counts. note: sometimes the transcript shows "KV cache" as "K V cache" — it's KV cache for attention cache.
[03:12] Samir: let's talk perf: our short chats are typically 128 tokens responses, typical seq len 256 incl prompt. p95 latency target 80ms. what config gets us there?
[03:24] Owen: if you go hosted at standard shared capacity, latency will be fine for many workloads but can vary. the Dedicated pools are where you get consistent p95 latency — pick a GPU class and pin a model; we can recommend batching window of ~8-12ms and small prefix caching to hit 60-70ms for your profile.
[03:46] Owen: also quantization: for embeddings and lower-precision generation, int8/awq variants cut cost but may increase latency slightly due to extra kernel ops; we'll show recommendations per model in Optimize.
[04:05] Diego: any surprises on prompt changes? we have a bunch of system message layering and tool calls.
[04:12] Maya: good question — most prompts port directly, but tokenizers differ: for instance, some anthropic tokens compress differently; we recommend running your prompt set through the tokenizer mapping script in the matrix to spot delta. also watch stop sequences behavior — minor differences.
[04:35] [06:00] Owen: demoing parity mapping spreadsheet — shows per-prompt token delta column, sample transformed prompt, and a sample scoring diff. we flagged prompts with >8% token delta.
[06:30] Samir: i see some prompts show 12% more tokens on redwood? what's the mitigation there?
[06:38] Owen: you can rewrite prompts or enable prefix caching; for repeated system prompts the KV cache avoids retransmission token costs. also some of our quantized variants change tokenizer boundaries, but those are rare.
[07:00] Lena: security again - do you provide SOC2 Type II certificate and iso?
[07:06] Maya: yes SOC2 is available, ISO 27001 in progress. we'll share a security pack with SOC2 report, pen test summary, and architecture diagram.
[07:22] Ava: SSO is critical — we use SAML and SCIM for provisioning.
[07:27] Owen: supported out of the box for Console RBAC — SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning. audit logs integrate with your SIEM.
[07:40] [09:00] Owen: moving on to console ops — showing route-level cost breakdown, per-token cost, and model-level latency histograms. you can set per-route quotas and token limits for throttling.
[09:20] Diego: can devs fallback to openai endpoints automatically if redwood is degraded? we have a hybrid strategy.
[09:27] Maya: yes, Smart routing supports policy-based fallback — you can say prefer Redwood, fallback to OpenAI or a cheaper regional model. we do recommend planning consistency.
[09:40] Samir: we run E2E tests and smoke checks - how do rollouts work for a canary?
[09:46] Owen: console supports canary percentages and auto-rollback on quality regressions tied to your eval set. also you can run A/B and drift detection.
[10:10] [12:00] Owen: now Optimize — intelligent batching suggestions: we analyze your traffic pattern and propose batching window, KV cache size, and quant profile. this often saves 15-35% on token unit cost.
[12:30] Samir: show an example where optimize reduced cost by 25%?
[12:36] Owen: yes, example customer "Zephyr" switched to prefix caching + int8 quant and saved 28% while keeping p95 within SLA. (note: names sometimes are transcribed wrong in notes).
[12:55] Lena: our embeddings workload is heavy - 600k embeddings/month. what about vector storage and similarity latency?
[13:03] Owen: Redwood Optimize suggests batched embed ops and caching hot vectors; for similarity we recommend approximate nearest neighbor cache on read path to shave ms. you can also use Dedicated for embeddings to avoid egress.
[13:28] Ava: about data residency - can logs be kept in-region?
[13:34] Maya: yes, we support region pinning for logs and model hosting. private deployments can keep data on-prem.
[13:50] Diego: cost model — can you give a back-of-envelope for our monthly usage?
[13:56] Owen: rough calc: with 600k embeddings and 2m generations at avg 150 tokens, and using recommended quant, you could see ~20% lower unit cost compared to your current mix; we'll provide a detailed breakout in the parity_matrix.
[14:20] Samir: any gotchas when porting function/tool calling? we have tool calls with structured json outputs.
[14:27] Owen: function calling is supported; watch for differences in the function schema enforcement. Redwood returns structured JSON but schema validation might be stricter; we include a shim for that. transcription sometimes shows "JSon" weirdly.
[14:45] [16:00] Lena: can we run a short benchmark? 7 days with a dedicated pool?
[16:05] Maya: yes, we can provision a 7-day trial Dedicated environment for benchmarking. we'll need your tokenized prompt set and expected traffic shape.
[16:18] Ava: what's the process for provisioning a VPC-connected Dedicated demo?
[16:22] Owen: step 1: exchange network peering info, step 2: KMS proof-of-possession for the key, step 3: we spin up a Dedicated pool in your region and provide endpoint. expect 3-5 business days for a VPC-enabled trial.
[16:40] Diego: ok that'll work.
[16:44] Samir: curious about model weights and licensing - do you host third-party weights or your own forks?
[16:50] Maya: we host curated open models and vendor-verified builds; for some commercial weights we can broker access under license. the parity matrix notes which models require additional licensing.
[17:05] [19:00] Owen: quick demo: run sample prompt through tokenizer tool in console — shows token count delta vs GPT4 and shows suggested rewrite to save 6% tokens.
[19:20] Samir: neat, can we integrate that into our CI?
[19:24] Owen: yes, the tokenizer/checker is available as a small CLI and api. we'll include sample GH actions in the repo.
[19:40] Lena: about SLOs — do you provide SLAs for Hosted vs Dedicated?
[19:46] Maya: Dedicated has SLA-backed latency and uptime; hosted is best-effort with region redundancy. detailed SLA and entitlements in enterprise contract.
[20:05] Ava: logging retention — how long for full request logs? we keep 1 year.
[20:12] Owen: logs retention configurable; enterprise plan supports extended retention, and you can stream logs to your SIEM for long-term storage.
[20:30] [22:00] Diego: any limitations on streaming large context windows? we do some 8k+ sequences.
[22:07] Owen: long contexts are supported; runtime picks kernels optimized for sequence length. very long contexts may increase memory and cost; we can recommend split strategies and cache reuse.
[22:35] Samir: what's the typical RMSE or hallucination differences? we mostly care about model fidelity.
[22:42] Owen: fidelity depends on model variant, we'll include eval comparisons on your prompt set — the QA in the matrix flags any regressions >3% and we can tune model choice or prompt rewrite.
[23:05] Lena: ok last thing - procurement timeline. we want pilot in Jan and decision in Feb.
[23:12] Maya: sounds reasonable; we'll aim to get trial provisioned this week and provide commercial T&Cs.
[23:22] Owen: i'll follow up with a Dedicated perf plan and cost worksheet.
[23:30] [25:00] Maya: recap — we'll share parity_matrix.xlsx, example curl and streaming shims, SOC2 pack, and set up a 7-day Dedicated trial. Outstanding: Pioneer to share prompt set and SRE contact.
[25:26] Lena: thanks, appreciate the actionable next steps.
[25:30] Diego: thanks everyone.
[25:35] [crosstalk]
[27:00] Owen: quick note: watch out for small naming differences in the matrix, e.g., "rdx-xl" vs "rdx-xl-quant" — choose based on perf tradeoffs.
[27:20] Samir: we'll pick a couple of high-volume flows for the benchmark.
[27:30] Ava: we'll need a runbook for the VPC peering and KMS exchange, can you send a template?
[27:36] Maya: yes, will attach peering runbook and KMS checklist.
[27:50] [30:00] Diego: any partner or vendor costs hidden? like egress or infra?
[30:08] Owen: egress costs depend on deployment type; for Dedicated in your VPC there is minimal egress, hosted might have standard cloud egress. we'll include breakout in the cost worksheet.
[30:30] Lena: thanks, we're good for now. excited to run benchmarks.
[30:40] Maya: great, last ask — who is our procurement contact? Diego?
[30:46] Diego: yes, DM me the contract stub.
[30:50] Maya: will do. thanks all.
[31:00] [end of recording — small talk follows for 2-3 minutes about holiday schedule, not captured fully in transcript]
